title: Bonded Claims: Bug Bounties for Product Labels
one_liner: Brands post a forfeitable bond behind a testable label claim, and anyone can buy the product, get it lab-tested and collect the bond if the claim is false.
customer: Mid-size DTC supplement, protein, baby-food and pet-food brands whose 'third-party tested' or 'heavy-metal free' claims are doubted, plus retail and marketplace buyers who want evidence and insurers.
problem: Label claims cannot be checked on the shelf. Certifications are one-time and paid for by the certified. Heavy-metal and potency class actions are routine, and gray-market peptide vendors forge certificates of analysis (FDA warning letters to seven online sellers, Mar 2026). Honest brands cannot distinguish themselves.
solution: A claim registry. The brand states a specific, machine-checkable claim (for example lead below X per serving, or label potency within 10%), posts a $10-50k bond in escrow and accepts a protocol: retail-purchased units, an accredited lab, and blinded replicates. Challengers pay for tests or use subsidised credits, and a neutral panel confirms chain of custody. A failed claim pays the challenger and forfeits the bond and badge. A claim that survives N challenges earns a 'survived challenge' tier that retail buyers can query by API.
why_now: Finnrick has now published 10,000+ independent peptide tests, proving that crowds will fund lab tests of vendors. Heavy-metal exposés and lawsuits keep recurring. Stablecoin and card-hold escrow make small bonds cheap to run. Retailers want a liability shield for clean-label shelves.
revenue_model: $2-5k annual listing fee, a 1-3% bond-management fee, challenge-processing fees, and retailer API licences.
non_obvious_insight: Bug bounties worked in software because they turn hostile sceptics into paid auditors. Physical-goods certification does the opposite and pays friendly auditors. A bond makes the brand fund the scepticism, and only honest brands can afford to post one, which gives the badge a real price premium.
first_30_days: Approach 10 clean-label brands that already publish certificates of analysis (creatine, collagen, omega-3, kids' vitamins) and pitch it as cheaper than class-action defence. Sign one ISO 17025 lab for a fixed test panel. Run a public 'challenge week' with a supplement community, using a standard escrow account.

title: Owner-Download: Capture Tacit Knowledge Before Sale
one_liner: Passively capture 60-90 days of an owner's calls, messages and jobs into a transferable playbook and a question-answering agent for the buyer.
customer: Owners aged 58+ of owner-dependent service and professional businesses ($300k-3M revenue) planning a sale in 12-36 months, plus the brokers who list them and the buyers who acquire them.
problem: Buyers discount hard for key-person dependency. The knowledge sits in the owner's head and phone: pricing instincts, customer quirks, vendor favors, unwritten rules. The traditional six-month handover rarely captures it.
solution: With consent, capture call recordings, texts and email, invoices, calendar and short weekly AI interviews. Produce SOPs, customer memory cards, learned pricing and quote logic, vendor scorecards and 'if X breaks, do Y' runbooks. The buyer gets a Q&A agent for year one ('how did the owner price gutters over 40 feet?') and the package goes in the data room as a transferable asset.
why_now: Long-context models, cheap call transcription and agentic retrieval make passive capture practical. Loosened SBA financing (up to $10M combined from July 2026) is drawing more first-time buyers who need this.
revenue_model: $2,500-6,000 per owner, broker referral fees, and a $199/month buyer subscription to the Q&A agent for 12 months.
non_obvious_insight: AI did not make this possible by automating the work but by making capture passive, so an owner no longer has to stop working to write manuals. Key-person discount is measurable, so the package can be priced against it.
first_30_days: Recruit five owners through two brokers in one vertical (HVAC, plumbing or landscaping). Run the capture pilots and ask buyers to rate the packages against a control listing on confidence and price.

title: Gate-Risk Radar for Evergreen Private Credit
one_liner: A quarterly shadow NAV and gate-probability score for every non-traded BDC and interval fund, sold to the RIAs and OCIOs who put clients into them.
customer: Independent RIAs and family offices ($100M to $3B AUM) with client money in non-traded BDCs, interval and tender-offer funds, at $400 to $1,500 per month per firm. Secondary buyers are TAMPs and wealth platforms (API license) and 401(k) advisers as alternatives enter defined-contribution plans.
problem: Advisers learn a fund has gated from a sponsor letter after the tender window closes. In Q1 2026 non-traded BDC investors requested about $13.9B and got about $7.4B. Blackstone gated BCRED in June 2026 with about 5% fills, and Q2 requests hit a record 12.4% of NAV with only 38% filled. Reported NAVs are smoothed, and nobody tells an adviser whether the next tender will be pro-rated or what to file.
solution: Ingest the tender-offer filings (window and cap), 10-Q and N-PORT marks, non-accruals and PIK share, listed-BDC discount to NAV, secondary bids on non-traded shares, and loan-index prices. Output three things per fund: (1) shadow NAV against reported NAV, (2) probability that the next tender gates and the expected fill rate, (3) a 'if I request X, expect to receive Y' calculator. Add compliance-ready client letters. Start as a public tracker of about 40 funds, then put the alerts and calculator behind a paywall.
why_now: 2026 is the first year pro-rata gating hit the whole non-traded BDC category. Blue Owl merged a non-traded BDC into its listed sibling under redemption pressure. The August 2025 executive order opening 401(k)s to alternatives is about to push far more retail money into these wrappers. Private-credit blowups in late 2025 turned advisers from curious to scared.
revenue_model: Tiered subscription for advisers, an enterprise API for wealth platforms and TAMPs, and a $250 per-fund 'client-ready due diligence memo' for compliance files.
non_obvious_insight: Pro-rata gating makes over-requesting the dominant strategy. Once investors expect a 14 to 38 cent fill, they file bigger requests than they need, so request size becomes a self-amplifying signal. It overstates true demand but predicts fill rates well. The gap between the listed-BDC discount and reported NAV leads request size by about a quarter. Quants see this as a bank-run game with strategic complements, not a credit-loss story, and nobody in wealth tech models it that way.
first_30_days: Scrape EDGAR tender-offer, 10-Q and N-PORT filings for about 40 funds and publish a free weekly 'gate watch' on LinkedIn and Substack framed as research. DM 100 RIA compliance heads and CIOs. Convert 10 to a $500-per-month pilot and start talks with two wealth-platform data teams.

title: Smell Graders for Recycled Plastic
one_liner: A network of trained human noses that gives every batch of post-consumer recycled plastic an odor grade from 1 to 5, creating the price tier and spec that brands need to hit recycled-content mandates.
customer: Plastic recyclers selling PCR resin (HDPE, PP), converters that mold bottles and tubs, and brand owners in personal care, household and food buying PCR under EU and US recycled-content rules. The recyclers' quality managers buy first, then brand procurement teams.
problem: Odor is one of the biggest barriers to using recycled plastic. Recyclers can't tell buyers reliably what a batch smells like. Brands reject loads or cap PCR percentages out of caution. Lab methods such as GC-olfactometry are slow and costly, and there's no shared odor grade the way coffee has the Q-score.
solution: A standard protocol (heated headspace jars, blind triplicates, a reference odor kit, descriptor vocabulary such as rancid, detergent, smoky) run by a panel of trained sniffers recruited from perfumers, coffee Q-graders, sommeliers and food-sensory panelists. Recyclers mail samples and get a 48-hour graded report. Human scores then train an e-nose and GC model that lowers cost per test. Over time it becomes a certification: license and train graders, and publish the grade spec brands cite in purchase contracts.
why_now: The EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation applies from 12 August 2026, with 2030 recycled-content minimums (30% for contact-sensitive PET, 10% for other contact-sensitive plastics). Brands have to buy far more PCR within a few years. Sensor vendors need human-panel labels to train on, and none has a standard odor tier to price against.
revenue_model: $120 to $250 per batch grade. Weekly-lot subscriptions for recyclers. Vendor-qualification programs for brands at $30k or more per year. Grader certification and training fees. Licensing of the labeled dataset to e-nose makers.
non_obvious_insight: Regulation mandates recycled content, but a human nose decides whether the resin is usable, and buyers will not trust a grade until someone standardizes it. Whoever owns the grading standard sets the price tiers for the whole PCR market, a bit like coffee's Q-grading. Human panels remain the legal and commercial ground truth even after e-noses arrive.
first_30_days: Recruit 12 sniffers from local specialty roasters and perfume or flavor schools. Buy vials, a hot plate and a reference odor kit for under $1,000. Offer three regional recyclers free grading of 20 batches each, and check the grades against their buyers' rejection history. Then price it. Publish a free 'PCR smell atlas' to attract recycler and brand inbound.

title: Licensed Cozy Games for Memory Care
one_liner: A turnkey activity program for senior living made of commercially licensed cozy indie games, in a kiosk kit that logs resident participation for compliance paperwork.
customer: Activity directors and operators of memory care, assisted living and skilled nursing communities, starting with independents and small regional chains of 5-50 sites. They pay about $199-349 a month per community plus a $349-499 kit.
problem: Nursing homes must run person-centered activity programs and document participation (CMS F-tag 679). Directors are short on budget and staff time. Existing tech is expensive proprietary hardware such as projector tables or VR. Consumer games are the wrong fit: their licences forbid commercial and public use, and they have reading-heavy UI, timers and fail states.
solution: A curated library of 30-50 indie titles that are gentle by design: no fail states, no timers, big targets, little text, familiar themes like gardening, cooking and tidying. Developers grant commercial, DRM-free licences for a revenue share. Each title runs in a locked kiosk launcher on a docked handheld or mini-PC to the TV, with big-button controllers. Staff get 5-minute group-play cards and a one-tap participation log that exports to activity documentation. It is positioned as activity programming, not therapy, so it makes no clinical claims.
why_now: About 4M Americans turn 65 each year through 2027, so demand for senior activities is rising. Handheld PCs are cheap and reliable. Senior living operators are already piloting games (for example the Belmont Village pilot of a cognitive game). Steam's glut of cozy games means many strong titles with dormant back-catalogs that earn nothing.
revenue_model: Monthly subscription per community, a hardware kit margin, and 40-50% of subscription revenue paid to developers by playtime. Later: enterprise contracts with chains, and reimbursement or wellness-budget channels.
non_obvious_insight: Steam keys are personal-use licences. Only the developer can grant commercial or public-performance rights, and a dormant catalog makes them say yes for a small guarantee. The traits that make cozy games sell are exactly what dementia-friendly design needs. And directors buy relief from documentation and set-up time, not cognitive outcomes. VCs file this under 'brain-training edtech', while an insider sees a licensing arbitrage plus a compliance workflow.
first_30_days: License 8-10 cozy titles, offering $500 minimum guarantees plus revenue share. Assemble 5 kits at about $400 each. Offer free 4-week pilots to 5 local communities through activity-director Facebook groups and state activity-professional associations. Log participation minutes per resident. Convert pilots to paid at week 5.

title: Pallet Co-Op for Micro-Resellers
one_liner: A distributor for one-person resellers that buys store-closing truckloads, values them SKU by SKU, and splits them into size-matched $150 to $500 shares delivered to each member.
customer: Under-25 and hobbyist resellers (roughly 3 to 100 sales per week) who currently buy at retail or from other resellers. They pay a markup of 8% to 15% plus a $19 per month membership.
problem: Real wholesale margins are locked behind minimum order quantities and size-run mismatch. A liquidator lot has 240 pairs, but 60% are size 6 or size 13 that nobody wants to hold. Mystery pallets are priced as a percentage of MSRP, not by what a SKU actually resells for, so buyers overpay for junk and underbid the winners. Discord 'group buys' exist but run on trust and screenshots, and they collapse when someone ghosts on payment.
solution: We buy truckload and pallet lots from liquidators and closing retailers, run the manifest against resale comps to price every line, and slice it: each member gets a share of the SKUs and sizes they selected, with the top-value pairs allocated by lottery so nobody feels cheated. Deposits are collected before we buy, so we carry almost no inventory risk. A partnered 3PL or a garage-and-labels crew ships each member's slice within a week. Later: net-14 financing on shares and buy-back of unsold slow-moving sizes.
why_now: Retail contraction is producing a steady stream of liquidation lots in 2025-26: Foot Locker is being folded into Dick's with store consolidation, other mall and footwear chains are closing doors, and brands reset inventory after tariff and demand swings. Margins on hyped Nike pairs are thin, so only good buying keeps micro-resellers alive. Cheap vision models make manifest-to-comp valuation nearly free.
revenue_model: 8% to 15% markup on each share plus $19 per month membership. Later, interest on short-term inventory financing and fees for a 'sell-through insurance' tier.
non_obvious_insight: Capital is not what stops small resellers from wholesale. Break-bulk is. Nobody sells a truckload in 40 slices sorted by size. The person who does the boring sorting, allocating and shipping becomes the small reseller's Costco. Because valuation uses resale comps rather than MSRP percent, the co-op can quietly outbid mystery-pallet buyers on the best lots.
first_30_days: Find one liquidator willing to sell a 5 to 10 pallet lot of mixed sneakers and apparel. Pre-sell 40 slots at $250 each in a Discord with deposits before buying anything, using the manifest value as the pitch. Rent a garage or use a local prep center. Ship in 10 days, collect testimonials and reviews, then run the next lot every week.

title: Capacity-Attested Wishes Recordings for Estate Attorneys
one_liner: Elder-law attorneys add a clinician-scored capacity note and a hash-sealed, attorney-controlled recording of the client's stated wishes to every will or trust signing, so heirs cannot wave the evidence away as a deepfake or as undue influence.
customer: Solo and small-firm elder-law and estate attorneys (they pay per client and mark it up), plus trust companies and bank wealth desks that handle contested-estate risk.
problem: A roughly $6T wealth transfer is under way, probate and estate cases rose about 32% from 2020 to 2024, and the heirs are Gen X and millennial executors. Cheap voice and video cloning means any real recording of 'what Dad said' can now be dismissed as fake, and undue-influence contests keep coming. Many attorneys avoid video because a shaky performance can backfire. Solo agers with no family have nobody to vouch for their wishes at all.
solution: A packaged signing workflow. (1) A 20-minute structured capacity assessment by a telehealth geriatric nurse practitioner or neuropsychologist, timed to the signing day. (2) A guided recording captured in an app that signs at capture with device attestation and a C2PA-style manifest, plus an independent RFC 3161 timestamp. The attorney decides what is retained. (3) An escrow vault that releases to the named executor on receipt of a death certificate. Output is a one-page verification link a probate judge can check without trusting the platform.
why_now: The oldest boomers turned 80 in 2026. FDA-cleared Alzheimer's blood tests (May and Oct 2025) will create a large biomarker-positive but still-competent population whose later wills will be attacked. C2PA 2.3 is mature and TikTok joined in Jul 2026. Voice cloning is good enough that courts and opposing counsel will start treating unsigned recordings as suspect.
revenue_model: $295-495 per client package billed to the law firm (clinician gets about $120, the rest is platform revenue), $99 a month per firm for vault storage and verification links, and later an enterprise tier for trust companies. Long-term escrow storage fees are recurring.
non_obvious_insight: The valuable evidence is not the video. It is a contemporaneous capacity finding made during the pre-dementia 'lucid window' that blood-test diagnosis is about to make very common. Provenance tech simply makes that finding, and the wishes on record, impossible to dismiss as synthetic. Attorneys buy this as malpractice and litigation insurance, not as a media product.
first_30_days: Sign 3 to 5 elder-law firms as design partners through state bar elder-law sections. Contract two geriatric NPs at a per-assessment fee. Build the capture app on off-the-shelf C2PA and timestamping libraries. Run 10 live signings at a discounted $195 and turn each into a case study for the next firm.

title: Coolant Assay Lab for Liquid-Cooled GPU Racks
one_liner: Oil analysis for GPU clusters: mail-in and inline coolant testing that catches corrosion and biofilm before they kill racks, and produces the neutral evidence for warranty fights.
customer: Neoclouds, colocation operators and enterprise AI teams running 1-50 MW with direct-to-chip liquid cooling. Insurers and lenders are second-wave buyers.
problem: Rack densities past 100 kW make liquid loops mandatory, and hundreds of small operators are running them for the first time. Their expertise is IT, not fluid chemistry. Glycol degradation, galvanic corrosion, dissolved copper and biofilm clog cold-plate microchannels and cause slow thermal throttling or sudden leaks. When a failure happens, the rack OEM, CDU vendor, coolant supplier and colo each blame the others and nobody has data.
solution: Sample kits and an inline sample-port sensor puck for every coolant distribution unit loop. A partnered industrial fluids lab runs standard assays: inhibitor level, pH, conductivity, particle count, bacteria, and metals. The software trends each loop and flags drift. A chain-of-custody Coolant Passport records every sample. Add dispatch of a flush-and-refill crew when a loop fails a threshold.
why_now: Next-generation rack systems shipping in 2026 assume liquid cooling by default, and operators are retrofitting halls that were never plumbed for it. The wave of first-time operators is happening now, before standards exist.
revenue_model: $400-1,200 per loop per quarter for assay and trending. $3-10k per emergency flush dispatch. Later, data licensing to insurers and OEMs for warranty and underwriting.
non_obvious_insight: The failures will come from boring chemistry, not from chips. Whoever holds the longitudinal sample history holds the evidence in every warranty dispute, and becomes the de facto standard, the way engine oil labs did for fleets and aviation.
first_30_days: Partner with an existing industrial fluids lab in Texas or Virginia that runs ASTM methods. Offer three small neoclouds a free first assay in exchange for read access to their thermal telemetry. Publish a short field guide on loop failure modes. Convert those three to a paid quarterly plan.

title: Ceiling-Camera Auto-Logging for Strength Gyms
one_liner: Cameras that watch the lifting floor and automatically log every athlete's sets, reps, load and bar speed with no phone.
customer: Independent strength gyms, CrossFit boxes, powerlifting clubs and high school and college weight rooms paying $199-499 per month.
problem: Progress tracking is the strongest retention lever in lifting, but manual logging is tedious so most members skip it, and coaches at high athlete ratios cannot see everyone's sets or spot stalls.
solution: Two to four ceiling cameras plus an edge box; vision models recognize the exercise, plate colors (load), rep count and bar velocity; lifters are identified by wristband or QR rather than faces; a coach dashboard flags stalls, form drift and missed sessions and a member app fills logs automatically.
why_now: 2025-26 vision foundation models handle exercise and object recognition at the edge on cheap hardware, and tightening biometric privacy laws push products toward non-facial identification.
revenue_model: $199-499 per gym per month plus $1.5-3k install; school weight-room licenses; velocity-based-training analytics as an add-on.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer is the coach or owner, not the member: automatic logging gives coaches visibility that drives retention and coaching upsells, a Hudl for the weight room. Avoiding face recognition sidesteps biometric-law exposure.
first_30_days: Install DIY hardware (about $800) in two friendly gyms, label two weeks of squat, bench and deadlift footage with plate detection, offer a free three-month pilot, and measure log completion and member retention to justify $299 per month.

title: Transformer-Level VPP That Defers Replacements
one_liner: Orchestrate home batteries, water heaters and chargers under each overloaded transformer, and get paid by the utility for every replacement you delay.
customer: Rural co-ops and municipal utilities facing 128-week transformer lead times, with investor-owned utilities later. The utility pays per transformer-year of deferral.
problem: Over 40M distribution transformers are past service life and new EVs and heat pumps overload them. Lead times are long and prices are up sharply. Today's VPPs dispatch at system level and ignore which transformer is constrained.
solution: Join each enrolled device to its transformer using AMI and GIS data, forecast loading, and dispatch flexible devices to keep every unit under its thermal limit. Guarantee performance with a penalty, and offer participating homes discounted batteries or controllers. Start with cheap loads (thermostats, water heaters, EV chargers) before batteries.
why_now: Transformer lead times, a 46% storage attach rate, proven large-scale dispatch, wide AMI deployment and mature DER standards (IEEE 2030.5, OpenADR 3).
revenue_model: $1-3k per transformer per year deferral fee versus $15-40k replacement cost, plus SaaS and VPP energy revenue share.
non_obvious_insight: VPPs are sold on system capacity, but the utility's scarcest asset is local: the pad-mount unit. Flexibility at the right node beats megawatts at the wrong one.
first_30_days: Sign one co-op with AMI data. Analyze it to find ~50 near-limit transformers. Propose a 90-day pilot with about 200 homes starting with thermostats, water heaters and chargers. Use measured loading reduction as the success metric.

title: Shelf Zero: Unclaimed Cremains Clearance Service
one_liner: A done-for-you compliance service that legally and respectfully empties the closet of unclaimed ashes that nearly every funeral home and crematory is afraid to touch.
customer: Independent funeral homes and crematories, where the owner or office manager pays per container. Secondary buyers are county public administrators and medical examiner offices. A third group is owners preparing to sell, whose buyers will flag the shelf in diligence.
problem: Cremation is now the majority disposition and still climbing. Families ghost after the cremation: an unpaid balance, an estrangement, a move, or a death of the only relative. State law on unclaimed remains varies widely. Search results show, for example, 120 days after written notice in Minnesota, at least 121 days in Texas, 60 days in Ohio and Nebraska, and 90 days with cemetery-contract rules in California. Directors won't scatter anything without a bulletproof paper trail, because one angry cousin surfacing four years later is a lawsuit or a board complaint. So the boxes pile up. A two-generation-old home can have dozens or hundreds, and staff feel guilt every time they walk past the shelf.
solution: A per-state playbook run as a service. Intake is a spreadsheet upload of name, date, contract and contact. Then skip-tracing for next of kin and authorizing agents, certified-mail and email notices on the statutory timeline, and a timestamped evidence file. Lawful disposition follows, through partner columbarium common niches, scattering gardens or sea scattering, each with a signed Certificate of Lawful Disposition per box. Veterans are identified through records requests and routed to the free national-cemetery inurnment route and Missing in America Project-type volunteers. Families who surface late can still reclaim through the funeral home for a small fee. An ongoing alert that flags containers at day 30, 60 and 90 stops the shelf refilling.
why_now: Cremation share keeps rising and household budgets are stretched, so abandonment is increasing. Consolidators such as SCI keep buying independents (about 22 funeral homes and 2 cemeteries for roughly $101M in 2025 per its filings). Their diligence treats an uncleared shelf as a liability, so retiring third-generation owners suddenly need a clean inventory. Skip-tracing and document automation are now cheap enough to run per box at a profit.
revenue_model: $175-$400 per container, tiered by state notice complexity. A $1,500-$3,000 pre-sale shelf audit and clearance bundle sells to owners about to list. A $49-$99/month ongoing aging-alert subscription covers new cases. Disposition partner fees (niche, scattering, transport) are passed through with a margin.
non_obvious_insight: The problem isn't the ashes, it's the paper trail. Nobody wants to be the person who scattered too early, so the shelf grows for decades. Outsiders assume it's a handful of boxes and a sad footnote. Inside, it's a compounding legal and emotional liability that every owner would pay a flat fee to make disappear, and the product being sold is really indemnifying documentation plus dignity, not disposal logistics.
first_30_days: Pick Ohio, Minnesota and Texas, where statutory safe harbors are clearest. Pay a funeral-law attorney a few thousand dollars to draft the three state notice templates and the disposition certificate. Offer a free 'shelf audit' to 30 homes via the state funeral directors' association newsletter and the private director Facebook groups. Convert five homes at $250 per box as pilots. Sign one local columbarium or church for a common-niche arrangement and one veterans-remains volunteer chapter.

title: Hard-Stop Fuse and Warranty for AI Cloud Bills
one_liner: A free scanner finds unrestricted legacy Google/Firebase and Bedrock exposure, installs a real hard kill-switch, and later sells a capped bill-shock warranty only to accounts that have the fuse installed.
customer: Seed-stage startups, solo developers and small agencies running LLM calls on GCP/Firebase or AWS Bedrock, including anyone running coding agents unattended. They pay $29-49/month per cloud account for the fuse and monitoring, and a small warranty premium later.
problem: Cloud providers ship alerts and credits, not hard caps, and they often refuse refunds. A Bedrock user ran up $37,901.73 through a LiteLLM + prompt-caching miss and asked 'why can I not say this IAM principal may spend at most $200/month'. A 2016 Firebase Android key generated $67k of Gemini charges in 19 hours, and Google support said it was 'unable to make adjustments'. A Claude Code user burned $2,000+ without noticing. A founder's $4,200 fraudulent Gemini charge was followed by suspension of a $1M ARR company's whole Google Cloud project.
solution: Step 1, a read-only CLI/web scanner that lists unrestricted API keys, projects with Gemini or Bedrock enabled, forgotten legacy Firebase keys (which the May 2024 auto-restriction policy missed in at least one documented case), and missing budget actions. Step 2, a one-click installer for hard stops: key restrictions and quota overrides on GCP, and on AWS Budget Actions that attach an IAM/SCP deny on model invocation. Step 3, per-minute anomaly detection that trips the fuse in seconds, not at the next daily billing rollup. Step 4, once an account has run fused for 30+ days, a capped bill-shock warranty (start at $5k, backed by a small reserve, later an MGA or reinsurer) priced from the loss data the fuse collects.
why_now: Unattended agents with huge contexts and Opus-class pricing turned ordinary integration mistakes into five-figure invoices in 2026. Gemini access now hangs off keys created years before Gemini existed. Google and AWS are visibly not shipping hard caps: the April 2026 $67k Gemini case was denied adjustment as of May 2026, and the $37.9k Bedrock case is from April 2026.
revenue_model: Free scan (lead gen). $29/month per cloud account for fuse plus monitoring, $49 for multi-project agencies. $199 one-off audit-and-install for agencies. Warranty add-on priced at roughly 2-4% of the covered limit per year, sold only to fused accounts.
non_obvious_insight: The clouds have shown the market will not get hard caps or reliable refunds from them, so the insurable unit is a fused account, not a customer. The technical control doubles as underwriting, and every victim thread is a warm lead. Evidence: $37,901.73 Bedrock bill with the 'hard spend limit' complaint https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47933355; $67k in 19 hours with Google denying adjustment and other victims reporting $13,000 and £2,700 https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/unexpected-67k-gemini-api-spike-in-19-hours-2016-firebase-provisioned-android-key-not-covered-by-googles-may-2024-auto-restriction-policy/142717; $1M ARR startup suspended after a compromised key https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48396596; $2,000+ Claude Code invoice https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46851021. Caveat: refunds are not reliably obtainable, so do not lead with a claims-desk model.
first_30_days: Week 1-2: build the GCP key/Gemini exposure scanner on top of Cloud Asset Inventory and publish 'Check your 2016 Firebase keys' on HN and the Google AI forum thread. Week 3: add an AWS CloudFormation one-click Budget Action deny for Bedrock. Week 4: DM the authors and repliers of the public bill-shock threads, plus agencies, and offer a $199 audit-and-install to the first 20; convert them to $29/month monitoring. Log every trip event and near-miss to build the actuarial base for the warranty.

title: Preflight Lab for Steam Frame Verified
one_liner: A shared hardware lab that runs your build on real Steam Frame, Steam Machine and Deck units, finds why it would fail Valve's compatibility review, and fixes it.
customer: Back-catalog publishers with 20-200 older titles, and mid-size indie studios that want the 'Great on Frame' or Steam Machine badge. They pay $250-1,500 per title for preflight plus fix, or $1-3k a month for catalog coverage.
problem: The Steam Frame is an ARM device that runs x86 games through FEX and Proton, and it launched in mid-September 2026. Only about 131 titles were Verified at launch out of tens of thousands. Valve's review is a queue with terse pass/fail notes, and each resubmission costs weeks. Failures are usually boring: launcher windows, first-run dialogs, 32-bit dependencies, cutscene codecs, kernel anti-cheat, controller glyphs, unreadable text, missing the 30fps at 720p floor. Devs can't justify buying a $1,059 headset to test.
solution: A rack of real devices with an automated runner. It launches the build through Steam, drives it with synthetic controller input, and records frame-times. It OCRs UI text height, uses a vision model to catch launcher and dialog windows, and checks the checklist Valve publishes. The output is a ranked punch-list. A paid fix-it tier handles launch options, Steam Input configs, codec swaps and small patches, then resubmits to Valve.
why_now: Steam Machine (June 29, 2026) and Steam Frame (September 2026) just shipped, with FEX and the verified-badge process brand new. The first 6-12 months of a new Valve platform are when badges are scarce and the store gives them the most weight, as happened with Deck Verified in 2022. Back-catalog publishers will want to opt in whole catalogs at once.
revenue_model: Per-title preflight and fix fees, catalog subscriptions for publishers, and a success-based 'Verified or partial refund' premium tier.
non_obvious_insight: The failures repeat across titles, so a publisher with 60 games amortizes every fix, and a lab that has fixed one FMV codec problem fixes it for a hundred games. Studios also can't afford the hardware, so shared capex becomes their opex. Triage by expected Frame-owner overlap, because the badge only pays off in genres that owners actually buy.
first_30_days: Buy 2 Frames, 1 Machine and 1 Deck (about $3.5-4k). Run 10 free preflights for devs recruited from Steam Frame and Deck communities and Linux gaming press. Publish 'the top 10 reasons Frame review fails', drawn from those real runs. Pitch 5 ports and back-catalog publishers a fixed price per title for a 20-title pilot.

title: Court-Accounting Software for Family Conservators and Executors
one_liner: Statement-to-court-form automation for family members who must file annual accountings for a parent under conservatorship or through probate.
customer: Lay conservators, guardians and executors (Gen X children), plus probate attorneys, CPAs and professional fiduciaries who handle 20-200 cases.
problem: Roughly a million-plus adults are under guardianship or conservatorship, and probate cases rose about 32% from 2020 to 2024. Appointed family members must file county- and state-specific accountings with receipts and categories. Errors mean surcharges or removal, and lawyers or accountants charge $500-2,500 a filing.
solution: Connect bank accounts or upload statements, categorize against the state's court forms, flag court-sensitive items (gifts, related-party payments, unusual withdrawals), produce the accounting and receipt binder, and calendar deadlines. Include optional attorney review. Launch in California and Texas, where forms and rules are standardized.
why_now: 80+ growth means more incapacity and more estates. Elder fraud losses ($7.7B in 2025) are pushing courts to scrutinize guardians, and LLMs now parse statements accurately enough for categorization.
revenue_model: $399 a year per case for lay fiduciaries, and $79-150 per case per month for professional fiduciaries and law firms.
non_obvious_insight: Legal tech serves lawyers and estate-planning creation; nobody serves the family member who is legally required to be an amateur accountant. Court deadlines make the pain acute and the willingness to pay high.
first_30_days: Start with California and Texas. Build SEO around 'conservatorship accounting help', partner with probate attorneys, and sell the first 20 cases at $399.

title: Do-Not-Transact Registry: GAMSTOP for Scams
one_liner: An opt-in registry, controlled by consumers and their families, that crypto ATMs, gift-card sellers and wire desks must check before completing a high-risk transaction.
customer: Crypto-ATM operators and gift-card retailers (paying per check and for legal cover). People enroll for free through credit unions, senior centers and adult children.
problem: Crypto-ATM fraud losses rose 58% to $389M in 2025, 66% of it from victims aged 60+. Older adults lost $7.7B overall. Education campaigns fail because scammers coach victims mid-scam to bypass warnings. State AGs have sued major kiosk operators, and cities are considering bans.
solution: People (or a family member with their consent) register commitments made while calm: no cash-to-crypto, no gift cards above $X, no new-payee wires above $Y, bound to ID number and phone. Kiosks that already scan IDs, and retailers via API at gift-card purchase, check the registry and show a neutral refusal script. Lifting a block takes a 72-hour cooling-off period, which breaks the scammer's urgency.
why_now: State kiosk laws (daily caps, mandatory warnings, refunds) and AG lawsuits give operators an urgent need to prove diligence. IC3's 2025 data quantified the elder-loss concentration. Operators may soon need a defensible control to keep their licenses.
revenue_model: About $0.05-0.25 per check plus $500-2K per month per operator. Gift-card processors and retail chains by contract. Grants and credit-union sponsorships fund enrollment.
non_obvious_insight: UK self-exclusion for gambling works because people commit in a calm moment. Scam prevention has assumed you can persuade people mid-scam, which fails. A registry turns consumer protection into a B2B compliance lookup that operators buy for legal cover, so the payer is not the person at risk.
first_30_days: Build an enrollment page and a kiosk-check API. Pilot with one independent operator (100-500 kiosks) and one state credit-union league, and enroll the first 1,000 people through a credit union or senior center. Use the results to brief state legislators and the AG's office.

title: Original-Recording Music for Memory Care
one_liner: A playlist and licensing service for memory-care communities that matches each resident's favorites to the exact original master, and flags re-records, sound-alikes and AI covers that streaming catalogs are now full of.
customer: Memory-care and assisted-living operators (activity directors), adult day centers, home-care agencies and board-certified music therapists. Adult children pay for a family tier.
problem: Personalized music is one of the few low-cost tools that reaches people with dementia, but it depends on recognition of a specific, familiar recording. Streaming catalogs are riddled with 'greatest hits, re-recorded' versions, sound-alike compilations and now AI tracks. Deezer says over 50% of daily uploads are fully AI, and Sony has asked for 135,000+ impersonations to be removed. Understaffed activity directors cannot tell a 1966 master from a 2019 re-record, and facilities also carry public-performance licensing exposure.
solution: Intake asks a resident or family for songs, era, and where they danced or heard it. The software resolves each song to the original ISRC and audio fingerprint of the label master, rejects re-records, covers and AI-flagged tracks, and produces a device-ready playlist with the public-performance license bundled. Families can add human-made voice messages and personal recordings, stamped as verified human. Staff get a one-page 'response log' to note which tracks got reactions.
why_now: AI-track volume passed human uploads on Deezer in July 2026. Spotify, TIDAL and Bandcamp now label, demonetize or ban AI music, so machine-readable authenticity signals exist for the first time. Memory-care occupancy sits near a record 90%, the 80+ population is growing fast, and blood-test diagnosis pushes more families into post-diagnosis coping tools.
revenue_model: $99-199 a month per community, $12 a month for a family tier, and a per-seat licensing bundle where labels or collecting societies agree to a senior-living rate. Later, a B2B API for music therapists.
non_obvious_insight: In this setting the active ingredient is the exact recording rather than the song, and that is a provenance problem. The 'AI flood' harms the most vulnerable listeners because it degrades the catalog a caregiver assumes is authentic. The first pilot should test the hypothesis that covers and re-records underperform originals.
first_30_days: Build a resolver on public metadata (MusicBrainz, Discogs, label catalogs) and a fingerprint service. Offer a free 'playlist audit' to 10 memory-care communities and to Music & Memory-certified programs. Track staff-logged resident responses for original versus re-record and publish the result as your credibility asset.

title: Canary Humans: Leak-Testing ID Verification Vendors
one_liner: Put consenting, instrumented real people through a platform's ID and age checks, then prove whether the vendor kept, leaked or resold their documents.
customer: Trust-and-safety, privacy and vendor-risk leads at platforms that outsource ID or age checks (dating apps, gig and rental marketplaces, cannabis and vape retail tech, crypto exchanges, adult and gaming operators), and the cyber insurers underwriting them.
problem: Platforms pick verification vendors on a SOC 2 badge and a promise to delete images quickly, and customers cannot test that promise. AU10TIX, Discord's support vendor, Persona and IDScan were all breached in 2024-26. IDScan reported 150M+ licence scans stolen in Sept 2026. Ofcom and state AGs judge platforms on 'reasonable steps', so the platform owns its vendor's failure.
solution: Recruit a few hundred paid 'canary humans' with unique emails, phones, addresses and ID numbers, and enrol them in the customer's live verification flow with the customer's consent. Then run scheduled tests: deletion requests, access requests to the vendor and its sub-processors, and monitoring of breach dumps, data-broker files, phishing and spam lists and dark-market listings for canary-unique strings. The deliverable is a quarterly retention and leakage attestation with evidence, usable in vendor contracts, cyber-insurance applications and regulator files. It also produces a public 'retention half-life' benchmark by vendor.
why_now: IDScan's Sept 2026 breach (150M+ licences) and the Persona, AU10TIX and Discord-vendor incidents showed that certified vendors leak. The EU's 31 Dec 2026 age-verification rollout deadline will push thousands more sites to outsource checks. Ofcom has opened 90+ investigations and issued fines. The Delve scandal (Mar-Apr 2026) showed that paper compliance is not proof.
revenue_model: $25-100k per year per platform per vendor tested, an insurer portfolio programme (per-insured fee), and a breach-forensics retainer. Later add an efficacy-proof product for privacy-removal services.
non_obvious_insight: Compliance automation (Vanta is at roughly $300M ARR) certifies that controls exist on paper, and nobody tests outcomes. A verifier's product is a promise to forget, and the only way to audit a promise about data is to plant traceable data and watch where it surfaces. Security calls these honeytokens and direct marketers call them seed lists, but nobody has applied the trick to verification vendors.
first_30_days: Recruit 50 privacy-minded volunteers at $100-200 each with signed consent and a legal review (no fake IDs, real people only). Pitch three mid-size dating, gig or cannabis-tech platforms and one cyber MGA. Offer a free 90-day pilot against one vendor under NDA. Publish an anonymised benchmark from the pilot to generate inbound.

title: Remote-Piloted Robot Workcells for Returns Processing
one_liner: Two-arm teleoperated stations in US returns centers, piloted by trained remote workers in low-wage regions, priced per item and generating the data to automate each task over time.
customer: Reverse-logistics processors, e-commerce returns centers, refurbishers and 3PLs handling apparel and consumer electronics in high-wage regions.
problem: Returns are high-variance and every item is different, so they are labor-heavy, high-turnover and hard to automate. Pure autonomy is not ready and pure teleop is too slow: early stations may run at only 30-50% of human speed, so hourly pricing fails.
solution: Deploy open-source dual-arm stations (ALOHA-class, about $30k each) where remote pilots handle exceptions and supervise learned behaviors on routine items. Price per item processed, guaranteed 20-30% below local labor, and let one pilot cover 3-5 stations as autonomy improves. Every pilot hour becomes licensable training data.
why_now: Cheap arms, open-source teleop rigs and robot-learning models are good enough for supervised autonomy. XDOF's $50M annualized revenue shows the teleop-data market pays, and 1X's teleoperated NEO shows buyers already accept a human in the loop.
revenue_model: $0.40-1.20 per item processed, with data licensing to model developers as an additional revenue stream.
non_obvious_insight: The teleop-versus-autonomy debate is a false dichotomy for buyers who pay per outcome. The economic robot today is a pilot-supervised robot whose human share falls every month, so the transitional business earns money while producing the data rivals pay for. It only works if you price per item and measure interventions per hour honestly.
first_30_days: Partner with one returns processor. Deploy 2 open-source stations on 2 tasks (test and grade electronics accessories, re-bag apparel), recruit 6 pilots through a Philippine BPO partner, and sell a 90-day pilot at a per-item price.

title: Neutral Legacy Animal-Data Vault for NAM Validation
one_liner: A neutral data trust that turns pharma's shelved animal-study results into blinded concordance benchmarks organoid and organ-chip makers use to prove their methods are 'adequately validated.'
customer: Organoid, organ-chip and other NAM startups needing FDA-credible validation, CROs, and pharma tox groups that contribute data and earn credits.
problem: FDA's Sept 21, 2026 direct final rule swapped 'animal tests' for 'nonclinical tests' but requires methods to be 'adequately validated'. Its NAM use-case database has only 25 entries. Validation needs ground truth: in vivo and clinical outcomes for many compounds. That lives in competing pharma archives and old PDFs, and pharma cannot pool proprietary data across competitors.
solution: Contributors deposit outcomes for shelved or dead compounds (species, dose, target-organ findings, human outcome where known) into a trust with blinded, query-only access. NAM developers submit predictions on a blinded panel of 100-200 compounds. They receive sensitivity, specificity and PPV by context of use, in a format built for FDA meetings. Contributors earn free validation credits. Start from public sources: FDA and EMA review documents, NTP, open toxicogenomics sets and DILI ranking lists.
why_now: The FDA rule landed this week and the NAM database is thin. NIH turbulence pushes toward cheaper methods. The IMI eTOX project pooled 8,196 studies on 1,947 compounds from 13 pharma companies, which proves the sharing model can work, but it was a research consortium and not a validation product.
revenue_model: $20-100k per validation report, annual memberships ($50-150k for NAM vendors; $100k or in-kind data for pharma), and licensing of benchmark panels to CROs.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone treats animal data as obsolete. As new animal studies decline, the historical archive becomes a fixed, non-renewable supply and the only ground truth for validating replacements. Dead compounds carry no competitive risk, so the usual objection to sharing disappears. The owner of the concordance yardstick becomes a toll-taker on every NAM filing.
first_30_days: Assemble a public 150-compound reference set with animal and human outcomes. Sell 3-5 'pre-validation concordance reports' at $10-20k to organ-chip and organoid startups. Interview 5 pharma tox heads about pilot contributions of 20-50 shelved compounds each. Recruit a former FDA nonclinical reviewer as an advisor.

title: Small-Claims Autopilot for Unpaid Invoices
one_liner: Take a solo operator from unpaid invoice to demand letter, filing, service, hearing prep and enforcement in a self-help flow.
customer: Freelancers, contractors and small B2B suppliers with $1k-20k unpaid invoices and no lawyer.
problem: Chasing fails, lawyers cost more than the claim, and small-claims procedure (forms, service, evidence, hearing, enforcement) is confusing, so most owners write off the debt. Cash is tight: nonemployers are less likely to be profitable and lean on personal funds.
solution: Connect invoices, email and texts. The system builds an evidence timeline, verifies the debtor entity and registered agent through state records, drafts a statutory-interest demand letter, files via e-filing where supported, schedules service, and prepares a hearing script and enforcement steps (garnishment and lien templates). It runs as a self-help tool, with a partner attorney for contested cases.
why_now: LLMs read messy invoice and message threads, e-filing is expanding in many courts, and nonemployer cash flow is under stress.
revenue_model: $79 flat per claim plus 10-15% of amounts collected, or a subscription for repeat filers.
non_obvious_insight: The demand letter itself resolves a large share of cases, and enforcement of the judgment is where the value sits, so the product should cover the full path. The regulatory edge is self-help positioning and attorney partners (the FTC's DoNotPay order shows the limits; prior knowledge).
first_30_days: Pick two states with online filing and $10k-plus limits. Run 30 claims for freelancers and trades sourced from community groups, and publish recovery rates and time to payment.

title: Fractional Licensed Qualifier for Trade-Business Buyers
one_liner: Rent a vetted master-licensed professional as the bona fide qualifying officer, so first-time buyers of HVAC, plumbing, electrical and engineering firms can get financed and keep the license alive after the seller leaves.
customer: First-time acquirers (search funders, SBA-financed individual buyers, independent sponsors, small holdcos) of licensed-trade companies with $1-15M revenue. The buyer pays monthly. SBA lenders and business brokers are the referral channel.
problem: In licensed trades the license and credentials are the real asset, and they walk out the door with the seller at closing. Buyers without a license get rejected by banks, and a replacement certification takes 6-12 months. Search-fund and ETA (entrepreneurship through acquisition) volume is at record levels, so more non-credentialed buyers are chasing these businesses.
solution: A bench of retired or semi-retired license holders (master plumbers, electrical contractors, PEs, inspectors, HVAC qualifiers). Each is placed as a bona fide officer or employee under a state-specific structure with real supervisory duties, E&O cover and indemnity. The service comes with (1) a lender-ready 'credential continuity package' (letter, duties, key-person plan), (2) a 12-month program that sponsors an internal successor through exams and hours, and (3) a state-by-state compliance library. It operates only in states where counsel confirms the qualifier rules allow this. License-lending schemes are illegal in many states, so compliance is the moat.
why_now: About 100 new US/Canadian search funds launched in 2023 (record), and acquisition volume grew from $110M to $880M per Stanford data summarized on Wikipedia. More than half of US small-business owners are 55+ without succession plans. PE Hub's September 2026 feed shows continuing PE appetite for HVAC, pest control and vet add-ons, which lifts what owners of licensed businesses expect to be paid and pulls more of them into sale processes. Buyer supply now exceeds credentialed-buyer supply.
revenue_model: $2-4K/month retainer per placement for 12-24 months. $1.5-2.5K one-time lender package. Sponsored successor-certification program billed at cost plus margin. Later, group E&O and key-person insurance placement commissions.
non_obvious_insight: The binding constraint in trades acquisitions is the credential, not capital or price. Jack Rauch's Tew & Taylor deal was rejected by multiple banks because he had no building-code license or experience. Their words: 'you don't have this license, you don't have this experience... good luck. We won't touch it.' He had to close on family-office debt at a 33/33/33 cap table (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/jack-rauch-tew-taylor). Manolo Diaz Corrada's Bonneville deal names certifications as a single point of failure that take 'six months to a year to acquire' and are not economical to duplicate (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/manolo-diaz-corrada-bonneville-group). Nobody sells credential continuity as a product. Brokers treat it as the buyer's problem, and lenders treat it as a deal-killer. Caveat: the evidence is operator interviews with a small sample, and the legal structure must be validated state by state.
first_30_days: Pick two states with well-documented qualifier rules (for example FL and TX) and pay for a counsel memo on each. Recruit 10 retired license holders through trade associations, retiree groups and union alumni networks. Build a one-page lender-facing continuity plan and show it to 10-15 SBA lenders and 20 business brokers. Post the offer in ETA communities (Searchfunder, Acquiring Minds audience) and sign 2-3 buyers with signed LOIs for paid pilot placements at a discount in exchange for case studies.

title: Compliant Format Kit for Card-Break Sellers
one_liner: Counsel-designed formats and software that let breakers, repackers and game stores run randomized break and mystery-pack sales without tripping lottery law.
customer: Independent breakers and repack sellers on Whatnot, eBay and TikTok, plus game stores that run break nights.
problem: Random spot-assignment breaks are being attacked as illegal lotteries under California Penal Code 319. Fifteen arbitration demands were filed in March 2026 for 30+ clients (about 100 expected). A July 2025 suit names Whatnot and Fanatics Live, and a qui tam action was recently unsealed. Independent sellers carry exposure with no counsel and no tooling.
solution: Alternative formats (pick-your-own-team, guaranteed-value floors, no-purchase-necessary entry flows), a per-state rule engine with registration and bonding reminders, an audit-logged randomizer with retained video, age and spend-limit controls, odds-disclosure templates, and dispute-ready records.
why_now: Arbitrations run 12-18 months, so seller uncertainty peaks through 2027. Platforms are defending, not building seller tooling.
revenue_model: $79-299/month SaaS by seller volume, a legal-review add-on, compliance audits, and licensing to platforms.
non_obvious_insight: Litigation targets platforms, but the marginal legal risk sits with small sellers whose margins cannot absorb it. Nobody sells them a compliant product design, and the fix is to change the product (make assignment non-random or value-guaranteed), which software can standardize. Whether breaks are illegal is unsettled, so retain gaming counsel.
first_30_days: Retain consumer-gaming counsel. Publish a free state-by-state cheat sheet. Recruit 20 mid-size breakers through Discords and pilot a pick-your-spot format with a guaranteed floor at $99/month.

title: Emerging-Market Multigrade Methods for US Microschools
one_liner: License and adapt proven low-cost, paper-based, self-paced multigrade teaching systems from Colombia, Bangladesh and India, and sell them as a turnkey kit and training to US microschools and shrinking rural districts.
customer: Microschool founders and pod networks, including the roughly 1,000 microschools the brief says are in limbo awaiting federal scholarship-credit rules, paying $1,500-5,000 a year. Homeschool co-ops with ESA money and small rural districts forced into combined-grade classes are the next buyers.
problem: One adult with 6-25 kids across several ages is now the standard microschool model. Guides are often uncredentialed (about two-thirds at Alpha School), 48% of microschool students in one dataset have special needs, and most run on screens. 61% of teachers want less device use, and AI tutors have shown no benefit over plain practice in a two-year Tennessee study.
solution: Sequenced, printable learning guides for K-6 math and literacy, peer-tutoring routines, student-run classroom governance, a 2-day guide training plus six weekly remote coaching calls, and paper mastery checkpoints. The checkpoints double as evidence for scholarship-granting organizations and ESA administrators. Licence terms give originators such as Escuela Nueva (Colombia), BRAC's one-room schools (Bangladesh) or Rishi Valley's School in a Box (India) a royalty share, so the deal funds their work too.
why_now: The federal scholarship tax credit starts in 2027 with 31 states opted in and rules still unwritten, so founders are looking for defensible academics. K-12 enrollment is heading from 49.4M to 46.9M by 2031 and more than 1,000 schools closed this year, so multi-age classes are coming to ordinary rural districts. Screen fatigue, AI bans in NYC and LAUSD, and weak AI-tutor evidence all push buyers toward paper and evidence-backed methods.
revenue_model: A one-time kit plus training at $1,500-3,000 per microschool (about $300 per student), a $600-2,400 annual coaching subscription, and district pilots at $15-40k. Royalties of 10-15% go to the licensors.
non_obvious_insight: The US treats one-adult-many-ages classrooms as a Silicon Valley invention. Countries that built them out of necessity decades ago have field-tested materials that are cheap, paper-based, robust to bad connectivity and teacher-light. Those traits match what US buyers suddenly want in 2026: fewer screens, no AI dependence, and documented outcomes. The emerging-market side is the supplier of know-how, not the customer.
first_30_days: Contact the licensors and negotiate a one-subject pilot licence (grades 2-5 math) in English. Print five paper guide sets. Recruit five microschools through founder communities and networks like the National Microschooling Center at $1,200 each. Record baseline scores with NWEA MAP or i-Ready and re-test after 10 weeks so the results become the first case study.

title: Widowhood Risk Program Sold to Medicare Payers
one_liner: Use hospice's early knowledge that a caregiver spouse is about to become a widow to enroll them in a 180-day protective program, paid for by Medicare Advantage plans and ACOs.
customer: Medicare Advantage plans (especially those with dual-eligible special needs plans), ACOs and value-based primary care groups. Hospice agencies are the intake channel and receive a referral or administrative fee.
problem: The spouse of a hospice patient is the second patient, and nobody is paid to treat them. The caregiver spouse ran the pillbox, the checkbook, the driving and the meals. They have skipped their own appointments for months. In the weeks after the funeral their chronic conditions decompensate, and hospitalizations, ED visits and falls spike. The chaplain is the one person who sees the untouched pills, the empty refrigerator and the missed doctor visits. Payers only learn of the death through enrollment data that lags by weeks or months. Hospice bereavement services are a mailing program, and they do not bill for the spouse's medical risk.
solution: A two-part program. Before the death, a hospice chaplain or social worker flags a high-risk caregiver spouse using a 6-item checklist (medication management ownership, driving, isolation, own chronic conditions, missed visits) and refers them, with consent, to the program. After the death, a community health worker does a home visit within 72 hours, books a primary care appointment within 14 days, does a medication reconciliation, sets up meal delivery and transport, and runs structured check-ins at 2 weeks, 6 weeks and 6 months. The 6-week and 6-month checks include a prolonged grief screen (PG-13-R). Screen-positive people are referred to therapists trained in prolonged grief disorder treatment, billable to insurance because PGD has had its own diagnosis code (F43.81) since October 2022.
why_now: Medicare Advantage margins are under pressure, and plans are hunting for measurable avoidable-utilization programs and star-rating improvements. Value-based primary care and ACOs are expanding, and both are rewarded for preventing ED visits and admissions. Prolonged grief disorder became an official DSM-5-TR diagnosis in 2022, with an ICD-10-CM code from October 2022, so the treatment side is finally billable. Hospices are being asked to show quality beyond death itself. I could not verify current bereavement benefit designs at specific plans, so check that before pitching.
revenue_model: A per-enrolled-spouse fee of about $150 to $300 per month for 6 months, paid by the plan or ACO. This can convert to shared savings once there are a few hundred enrollees. Hospices receive a per-referral fee or a bereavement-outsourcing fee. Therapy referrals bill insurance directly, and the program can hold a small clinician panel. Employer benefit teams are a later channel.
non_obvious_insight: The highest-risk patient is not on the payer's radar and is not the patient the hospice is paid to look after. Only the hospice team knows the caregiver is fading, and it knows months before any claim or enrollment record does. The widowhood effect (well documented in the research literature, with elevated mortality and hospitalization in the months after a spouse dies) is an underpriced, predictable utilization event.
first_30_days: Pick one regional hospice and one value-based primary care group or small MA plan with a few thousand lives. Build the checklist and a simple spreadsheet workflow, then hire one community health worker or licensed social worker. Enroll the first 20 spouses at no charge, tracking ED visits, missed PCP visits and grief screens at 90 and 180 days. Use the data to sell a paid pilot to the plan or group before month 6. Get a HIPAA lawyer to sign off on the referral pathway and consent language.

title: Repatriation-of-Remains Concierge for Immigrant Families
one_liner: A fixed-price service that gets a loved one's body home across borders, and later a low-cost membership that pre-funds it.
customer: Immigrant families on one corridor at a time (for example US to Mexico or Central America, the Philippines, India or Nigeria), plus consulates, churches, mosques, community associations and funeral homes without international skills.
problem: Sending remains home costs thousands (often $5-15K, unverified) and requires consular paperwork, health permits, embalming, sealed caskets, air cargo rules and destination-side logistics. Families use GoFundMe, church collections and opaque middlemen, in days, while grieving.
solution: Intake in the family's language, document assembly (consulate forms, permits), a vetted network of embalmers, cargo forwarders and destination funeral homes, insurance and payment plans, and one coordinator. Later add a $8-$15/month repatriation membership underwritten through a licensed insurer partner.
why_now: Community payment and remittance rails are digital, translation and document assembly are cheap with AI, and immigrant communities are large and trust-network driven. Funeral homes treat this as an add-on they don't understand.
revenue_model: 15-25% service margin on $6-12K cases, membership fees, and insurer commissions.
non_obvious_insight: The mainstream industry treats repatriation as a sideline, but for these families it is the primary product. Corridor-specific know-how is the moat, and trust travels through churches and consulates.
first_30_days: Choose one corridor and one metro. Partner with a funeral home that already does it. Sign 3 churches or a consulate liaison. Run 5 cases at cost to document the exact process and price it.
